newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine reserves rise to $11.81 bln in April.
newsitem.headline: Philippine reserves rise to $11.81 bln in April.

text.p: The Philippines' gross international reserves were at $11.81 billion at the end of April against $11.75 billion at the end of December, the Central Bank said on Tuesday.
Despite the burden of servicing debts of the Central Bank as well as of the national government, reserves remained at a comfortable level, Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said in a statement.
The Central Bank was a net buyer of foreign exchange amounting to $1.04 billion, he said.
The bank's purchases from the foreign exchange market amounted to $1.87 billion representing 13 percent of the total transactions in the market, Singson said.
The Central Bank sold foreign exchange worth $831 billion.
The Central Bank said the figures for its foreign exchange activities were also for the same end-December to end-of-April period.
Singson said the $11.8 billion in reserves was sufficient to cover 3.1 months of imports of goods and services, or 4.5 months of merchandise imports.

The Central Bank said its net international reserves as of end of April stood at $10.485 billion, or $266 million higher than the agreed floor of $10.219 billion under the International Monetary Fund's extended fund facility.
